candidate_profile.description: The candidate sharply diagnoses private label mix as the core driver of stagnating profits, validates management's hypothesis with clean math, and gives a crisp recommendation that exceeds the target while addressing execution risk and future upside.
behaviour_rules: Begin with a concise recap and translate the target into a concrete $180M profit increase objective.
Use a sharp profitability framework that prioritizes mix and margin while ruling out store closures and short-term geographic expansion.
Infer from Exhibit #1 that historical profit growth tracked private label growth more closely than total revenue growth.
Clearly explain why private label margins are structurally better than national brands.
Perform the math cleanly: 3% of $60B revenue shifts to private label, multiplied by a 15-point gross margin uplift, then taxed at 30%, yielding about $189M of additional profit.
Conclude that management's plan meets and slightly exceeds the target.
Recommend pursuing the strategy while pressure-testing the 3-point shift assumption, validating one-time costs, and piloting the rollout.
Also note remaining upside from still trailing Trader Joe's on private label penetration, while acknowledging possible supplier and scale risks on national brands.

expected_issues: May not fully quantify second-order margin effects on the remaining national-brand assortment because the case only hints at them qualitatively.
Could still be pushed for a more detailed execution timeline, though the strategic recommendation should already be excellent.
expected_feedback_points: Excellent diagnosis that private label mix is the primary profitability lever.
Excellent use of the exhibit to connect private label growth and profit growth.
Excellent quantitative validation that the hypothesis exceeds the $180M target.
Excellent recognition of execution risks, one-time costs, and supplier implications.
Excellent recommendation to pilot, validate, and scale while preserving future upside.
